newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end down, near session lows.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end down, near session lows.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended lower, near session lows, after a late burst of profit-taking from longs.

Standard and Poor's 500 futures collapsed to a session low of 768.50 in the last minute or two of trading, fueled by technical weakness and disappointment that an afternoon bounce to midrange failed, traders said.
"Everyone took profits after hoping for a bounce," an S&P 500 trader said. "Monday it's going to be ugly for sure after this sloppy close," he said.
He put near-term downside potential to 764.50 and 762.50.
"This will go at least another five to seven handles lower," he said.

Several technicians said Friday's performance was a confirmation of Thursday when March rallied to a record high and then failed near the psychologically key 800.00 mark. The contract eventually slid as low as 774.00 on Thursday, a technically bearish key reversal.
Early on Friday, March easily added to losses and slid through support from Thursday's low.
"We're getting some wild swings and there's no liquidity in this pit," another S&P 500 trader said.
"It's brutal in there, people are skittish, but I think this is a buying opportunity," the trader said. "I am a buyer of dips."
Others agreed, saying the selloff was putting S&Ps back into more comfortable territory for new buyers.
Visiting downside targets as low as 740.00 and 720.00 would not impair the long-term uptrend, technicians said.

Volume was heavy. The Chicago Mercantile Exchange estimated S&P 500 futures volume on Friday at 99,667 contracts, compared with 86,084 traded on Thursday. The S&P volume record was set October 19, 1987, when 162,022 traded.
March S&Ps closed down 10.50 points at 769.75, KCBT Value Lines fell 3.65 to 698.85, NYSE Composites dropped 4.45 to 405.70, Nikkeis were down 235 at 17,500 and Nasdaq 100s fell 16.00 to 903.50.
